actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

facts.text: The repository describes itself as a comprehensive collection of robot URDF models.
The package's model is the MJCF scene go_bdx/scene.xml, whose root element is '<mujoco model="bdx scene">' and which includes go_bdx.xml on line 2.
The scene adds a gradient skybox, a checkered groundplane and a floor plane body to the included robot model.
The included model's root element is '<mujoco model="bdx">' and its compiler sets angle='radian', meshdir='meshes' and autolimits='true'.
The model's option line selects the implicitfast integrator; the timestep option on line 4 is commented out.
The bdx default class sets joint limited='true', and its six joint-parameter classes set range='-0.785398 0.785398'.
The bdx body declares a freejoint, and its pelvis body sets childclass 'bdx'.

The actuator section declares 16 position actuators with gear 1 and explicit ctrlrange values: the hip, knee, ankle and neck actuators use -30 to 30, the head actuators -5.55 to 5.55, and the antenna actuators -13.62 to 13.62.
The same actuator lines set forcerange -23.7 to 23.7 for the hip, knee, ankle and neck actuators, -7.3 to 7.3 for the head actuators and -0.2943 to 0.2943 for the antenna actuators.
The model declares six sensors on the imu site: orientation, position, angular velocity, linear velocity, linear acceleration and a magnetometer.
The mesh assets declare scale='0.001 0.001 0.001' for every STL mesh.
panda5_test/src/panda5.cpp initialises the ROS 1 node panda_visual and advertises joint_states and CPU-sample, mode and leg-end topics.

determinism.notes: The stand-in integrates the same placeholder response for the same controls from the model defaults; it has no seed input and its motion is not MuJoCo's physics, so no trajectory or state-hash replay is claimed.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it reads the MJCF for the joint dimensions, the actuator count and the per-actuator ctrlranges but integrates a placeholder first-order motion of each actuated hinge toward its control value, so trajectories, contacts, actuator kp/kv and forcerange dynamics and the floating base are not MuJoCo's
the stand-in ignores the joint ranges (-0.785398..0.785398) and moves a hinge toward any target inside the ctrlrange, where MuJoCo's joint limit would stop it
the freejoint is reset to zero qpos, not MuJoCo's model qpos0 (which would include an identity quaternion), and the stand-in resolves no contact, equality, tendon or sensor
no mesh or texture of the meshes/ directory is loaded and no sensor sample is exposed
the fake's 0.002 s timestep is a placeholder for MuJoCo's library default, not a bound from the clone; the stand-in offers no mj_getState/mj_setState, so its checkpoints copy placeholder arrays
the package serves the card's models[0] only, and no physical robot is modelled or driven

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
